verdict.rationale: Codex is a natural-language coding agent. Its docs say it can inspect code, run local commands, take an error screenshot with the prompt, split up a larger investigation across subagents, and use live web search to check external behavior. A hands-on community report says it "fixes everything" on hard problems, which corroborates this. Missing for 10: a dedicated first-party debugging/troubleshooting workflow doc (e.g., log or stack-trace analysis, debugger integration) and broader independent corroboration of debugging quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug issues and troubleshoot using natural-language queries

citations.quote: Pass an error screenshot, architecture diagram, or design reference with the first prompt, or paste an image into the interactive composer.
Split up a larger investigation — subagents: Ask Codex to delegate focused work to specialized agents, then bring their findings back into the main terminal session.
Inspect code, make changes, run commands, and automate repeatable work without leaving your terminal.
Switch a run to live web search when a task depends on current releases, documentation, or external behavior.
Then you spin the much slower GPT 5.3-Codex and it fixes everything in 3 minutes of doing the right thing.
